title: BatchedSpectralSmooth.lean

problem_class.label: nonconvex
problem_class.details: Unconstrained differentiable objectives on real m×n matrices, permitting nonconvexity, with a global lower bound fmin and f(x0)−fmin≤Δ.

oracle.label: stochastic_gradient
oracle.details: Jointly measurable, integrable, unbiased matrix-valued gradient samples g(x,ξ), with fresh IID seeds across individual oracle calls. Each sample counts as one call, including all samples within batches.

distinctive_assumptions.label: bounded_variance
distinctive_assumptions.details: There exists one fixed orthonormal row basis (b_i) and nonnegative σ_i with Σ_i σ_i≤s such that, uniformly in X, E‖(g(X,ξ)−∇f(X))ᵀb_i‖₂²≤σ_i². Neither independence between rows nor exponential tails is required.

distinctive_assumptions.label: non_euclidean_geometry
distinctive_assumptions.details: Spectral/nuclear dual geometry: ‖∇f(X)−∇f(Y)‖nuc≤L‖X−Y‖op. Allowed algorithms take constant-step polar directions of batch means.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BatchedSpectralSmooth.lean: spec.admissible, spec.allowedAlgorithm and batchedIterate; LongTails/Setups/FiniteVarianceSpectralSmooth.lean: spectralNorm, nuclearNorm and polar.

distinctive_assumptions.label: finite_dimensional
distinctive_assumptions.details: The ambient space is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin m × Fin n), identified with real m×n matrices; m,n are natural numbers.

distinctive_assumptions.label: other
distinctive_assumptions.details: Public information consists of m,n,L,Δ,s,ε,x0, with L>0, Δ≥0, s≥0 and ε>0. The objective, sampling law, row basis and individual σ_i are hidden. Oracle seeds are IID and independent of the algorithm seed.
distinctive_assumptions.evidence: LongTails/Setups/BatchedSpectralSmooth.lean: Public, spec.publicInput, spec.valid and spec.admissible; LongTails/Template.lean: Convergence.

accuracy.label: gradient_norm
accuracy.details: The measurable output must have integrable nuclear gradient norm and satisfy E‖∇f(output)‖nuc≤ε; the norm is not squared.

accuracy.label: expected
accuracy.details: Expectation is over algorithm and oracle randomness. The output is a uniformly selected iterate among x0,…,xT from the prescribed batched polar trajectory, after B(T+1) individual sample calls.

setup_category.label: non_standard
setup_category.reason: The formulation combines spectral-to-nuclear smoothness, a hidden fixed-basis row-variance profile, nuclear-norm expected stationarity and a prescribed batched polar algorithm family. Repository proofs and implementations were not inspected; the absence of a qualifying reference does not establish novelty.

descriptionHtml:
Batched Polar Matrix Optimization

We consider minimizing a differentiable, possibly nonconvex function f:Rm×n→R, where m,n are nonnegative integers. Its gradient is L-Lipschitz from the spectral norm to the nuclear norm, with L>0, and a given starting matrix x0 has objective gap at most Δ≥0 above a global lower bound. The oracle returns unbiased stochastic gradients using independent, identically distributed samples, with rowwise standard deviations summing to at most s≥0 in a fixed orthonormal basis. Batched polar updates must produce a random output x¯ satisfying E∥∇f(x¯)∥∗≤ε, where ∥⋅∥∗ is the nuclear norm, ε>0, and expectation includes sampling and algorithm randomness.

The optimization problem is infx∈Rm×nf(x). Equip the matrix space with the Frobenius inner product ⟨U,V⟩F=tr(U⊤V) and its norm ∥⋅∥F; gradients are taken with respect to this inner product. Write ∥⋅∥op for the induced Euclidean operator norm, also called the spectral norm. Its dual under the Frobenius pairing is the nuclear norm: ∥G∥∗=sup∥U∥op≤1⟨G,U⟩F. The algorithm receives m,n,L,Δ,s,ε, and x0; the objective and the oracle’s distributional model are accessible only through queries.

Our assumptions:

Assumption 1 (Spectral smoothness). The function f is Fréchet differentiable everywhere, and ∥∇f(x)−∇f(y)∥∗≤L∥x−y∥op,x,y∈Rm×n.

Assumption 2 (Lower bound and initial gap). There exists fmin∈R such that fmin≤f(x)for every x∈Rm×n,f(x0)−fmin≤Δ.

Assumption 3 (Unbiased oracle with a row variance profile). Let ν be a probability measure on a measurable sample space Ω. The oracle is specified by a jointly measurable map g:Rm×n×Ω→Rm×n. For every x, the random matrix g(x,ξ) is Bochner integrable for ξ∼ν, and Eξ∼ν[g(x,ξ)]=∇f(x). There exist a fixed orthonormal basis (bi)i=1m of Rm and numbers σi≥0 with ∑i=1mσi≤s. For every x and i, the vector (g(x,ξ)−∇f(x))⊤bi∈Rn belongs to L2(ν;Rn) and satisfies Eξ∼ν[∥(g(x,ξ)−∇f(x))⊤bi∥22]≤σi2. At call k≥0, a query x receives g(x,ξk), where the measurable sample variables (ξk)k≥0 are mutually independent with common law ν. Algorithm randomness is independent of the entire sample sequence.

Our formulation is algorithm-specific: we analyze batched polar updates. Define the polar direction as the minimum-Frobenius-norm maximizer of the linear objective over the spectral unit ball: S(G)=argmax∥U∥op≤1⟨G,U⟩F,polar(G)=argminU∈S(G)∥U∥F. The second minimizer is unique, including at rank-deficient G. The method chooses a constant step size η>0, a batch size B∈{1,2,…}, and an integer T≥0 from its inputs. Starting at the given x0, it makes B queries at each xt, for t=0,…,T, and follows Gt=1B∑j=0B−1g(xt,ξBt+j),xt+1=xt−ηpolar(Gt). These query and update rules must hold for every possible sequence of oracle replies. A measurable index J, drawn from the algorithm’s randomness independently of the samples, is uniform on {0,…,T}. After B(T+1) oracle calls, the output is x¯=xJ. The output remains xJ after any additional calls. The call count includes the batch at xT, although the output is selected from x0,…,xT.

Let P be the joint law of the algorithm randomness and the sample sequence. The output must be measurable, its gradient’s nuclear norm must be integrable under P, and the required accuracy is EP[∥∇f(x¯)∥∗]≤ε.

comparisonHtml:
Differentiable f:Rm×n→R satisfies ∥∇f(X)−∇f(Y)∥∗≤L∥X−Y∥op, f≥fmin and f(X0)−fmin≤Δ, with L,ε>0 and Δ,s≥0. The jointly measurable, integrable oracle G(X,ξ) uses IID samples and satisfies EG(X,ξ)=∇f(X). For a fixed orthonormal basis (bi)i=1m and σi≥0, E∥[G(X,ξ)−∇f(X)]⊤bi∥22≤σi2 and ∑iσi≤s. The setup requires constant-step, momentum-free batched polar updates and a uniformly selected iterate X^; the target is E∥∇f(X^)∥∗≤ε.

Batched Muon under BatchedSpectralSmooth.
Result Oracle complexity Novelty Limitations
(1) MuonNoiseSeparation (Ours) (review) O((1+s2/ε2)(1+LΔ/ε2))
(2) Muon (Tao et al. 2026, Theorem 4, v1) O(1+LΔε2+LΔ∥Σ∥∗2ε4). Restricted to E[NN⊤∣F]⪯Σ2. (1): Row-profile extension. For varying-sign rank-one noise, s=r=m≤n, ∥Σ∥∗≥rs: if r≥ε, LΔ≥ε2, costs are O(LΔr2/ε4) versus O(LΔr3/ε4). This improves the statement’s certification, not the method; see (3). (1): At s=∥Σ∥∗, extra s2/ε2 cost when s>ε, 2LΔ≤ε2. Requires IID samples and gradient-Lipschitz smoothness; (2) allows conditional sampling and a quadratic remainder bound.
(3) Derived bound (Tao et al. 2026, Appendix D.1) O(1+LΔε2+LΔs2ε4). Same row-profile model; substitute E∥N―B∥∗≤s/B. (1): Matches known rate for LΔ≥ε2; formal verification with explicit constants. Row-profile substitution leaves the descent argument unchanged. (1): Extra s2/ε2 cost when s>ε, 2LΔ≤ε2.

Abbr: Costs count individual stochastic-gradient calls, including every batch sample. ∥⋅∥∗: nuclear norm; ∥⋅∥op: spectral norm; N=G−∇f: noise; N―B: mean of B noise samples; Σ: fixed positive semidefinite covariance envelope; F: sampling history; r: number of rows in the varying-sign example.

source:
import LongTails.Setups.FiniteVarianceSpectralSmooth

namespace LongTails.Setups.BatchedSpectralSmooth

open MeasureTheory OracleTemplate
open LongTails.Algorithms.MatrixPolar

structure Public where
  m : ℕ
  n : ℕ
  L : ℝ
  Δ : ℝ
  s : ℝ
  ε : ℝ
  x0 : Space m n

noncomputable def batchMean {m n : ℕ} (B : ℕ) (reply : ℕ → Space m n) (t : ℕ) : Space m n :=
  (1 / (B : ℝ)) • ∑ j ∈ Finset.range B, reply (B * t + j)

noncomputable def batchedIterate {m n : ℕ} (direction : Space m n → Space m n) (η : ℝ) (B : ℕ)
    (x0 : Space m n) (reply : ℕ → Space m n) : ℕ → Space m n
  | 0 => x0
  | t + 1 => batchedIterate direction η B x0 reply t - η • direction (batchMean B reply t)

def FollowsBatched {m n : ℕ} (direction : Space m n → Space m n) (η : ℝ) (B T : ℕ)
    (x0 : Space m n) (A : Algorithm (Space m n) (Space m n) (Space m n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ draw : A.Seed → Fin (T + 1), Measurable draw ∧
    Measure.map draw (A.law : Measure _) = (PMF.uniformOfFintype (Fin (T + 1))).toMeasure ∧
    ∀ seed reply,
      let state := LongTails.Setups.FiniteVarianceSpectralSmooth.replyState A seed reply
      (∀ t j, t ≤ T → j < B →
        (A.query (state (B * t + j))).2 = batchedIterate direction η B x0 reply t) ∧
      ∀ extra, A.output (state (B * (T + 1) + extra)) =
        batchedIterate direction η B x0 reply (draw seed)

abbrev spec : Setup where
  Params := Public
  Public := Public
  Instance p := Space p.m p.n → ℝ
  Query p := Space p.m p.n
  Reply p := Space p.m p.n
  Output p := Space p.m p.n
  publicInput p := p
  valid p := 0 < p.L ∧ 0 ≤ p.Δ ∧ 0 ≤ p.s ∧ 0 < p.ε
  admissible p f O :=
    (∀ x, HasGradientAt f (gradient f x) x) ∧
    (∀ x y, nuclearNorm (gradient f x - gradient f y) ≤ p.L * spectralNorm (x - y)) ∧
    (∃ fmin : ℝ, (∀ x, fmin ≤ f x) ∧ f p.x0 - fmin ≤ p.Δ) ∧
    ∃ (model : LongTails.Setups.FiniteVarianceSpectralSmooth.GradientModel f p.s)
      (P : ProbabilityMeasure (ℕ → model.Ω)),
      LongTails.Setups.StochasticGeneralizedSmoothAndConvex.IID
        (fun k (ξ : ℕ → model.Ω) => ξ k) (model.law : Measure model.Ω) (P : Measure _) ∧
      O = { Seed := fun _ => model.Ω
            law := P
            answer := fun _ (_, x) ω => model.sample x ω }
  successful p f output P :=
    Measurable output ∧
      Integrable (fun ω => nuclearNorm (gradient f (output ω))) (P : Measure _) ∧
      (∫ ω, nuclearNorm (gradient f (output ω)) ∂(P : Measure _)) ≤ p.ε
  allowedAlgorithm p A :=
    ∃ (η : ℝ) (B T : ℕ), 0 < η ∧ 0 < B ∧ FollowsBatched polar η B T p.x0 A

end LongTails.Setups.BatchedSpectralSmooth
